quarterly_data.signal: FY ending March 2027 forecast (CEO Hitoshi Saito): consolidated net sales of 146,300 million yen, up 6% YoY, and operating income of 34,300 million yen, up 5%; Electronics net sales +7% and operating income +7% (mainly reflecting higher R&D expenses within SG&A), Medical and Pharmaceuticals net sales +3% and operating income -21%; exchange-rate assumption 150 yen to the U.S. dollar; first-half and second-half figures almost at the same level. Concerns over rising raw material costs and procurement difficulties from the Middle East situation are not factored into the forecast, and possible tender-offer expenses cannot yet be estimated. CFO Sayaka Tomioka: although the Electronics mix is improving, additional costs on top of higher R&D are expected, so the Electronics operating margin is assumed to be flat.
quarterly_data.figure: FY ending March 2027 forecast: net sales 146,300 million yen (+6%); operating income 34,300 million yen (+5%); Electronics sales +7%, operating income +7%; 150 yen to the U.S. dollar

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics demand (CEO Hitoshi Saito): in FY ended March 2026 materials for PKG substrates benefited from dramatic volume growth in dry film (DF) products for memory applications under AI-backed demand; on the net-sales-by-product slide (quarterly trends), DF products for PKG substrates performed extremely well, up 32% YoY, and regular materials for rigid boards rose 1% YoY after a review of focus product areas. For FY ending March 2027 the company expects higher PKG substrate material volumes as memory-application demand stays above past levels on AI proliferation; flat rigid-board liquid material volumes despite moderate automotive growth; and a further decline in white DF products for Mini LED displays. Q&A: PKG substrate materials for memory are increasing under AI demand and rigid-board materials are also growing considerably (used in automotive and AI server applications, so the growth is hard to pin down); the increase in DF for PKG substrates can be assumed to be largely due to AI demand (the memory increase itself is not disclosed). CFO: white DF will not fall to zero, as customers' current final-product models still use Mini LEDs.
quarterly_data.figure: DF products for PKG substrates +32% YoY; rigid-board regular materials +1% YoY (net sales by product)

quarterly_data.signal: Supply and procurement (CEO Hitoshi Saito, Q&A): no notable customer pull-in of orders; the company is securing capacity to maintain a stable and fair supply system. From the Middle East situation, concerns over resins and solvents are appearing in some areas - the company acted early and is evaluating substitutes; sub-materials such as plastic containers and films are also affected and are being handled through inventory buildup and substitutes; letters were sent to customers saying supply concerns may arise between June and July, and the letters state the company intends to pass higher costs on by raising product prices. Japan is affected the most (other regions use different suppliers, so localization disperses procurement risk); substitute containers have already been shipped to some customers for evaluation, and customers say they intend to respond swiftly even though high-end PKG substrate materials undergo strict evaluation. CFO Sayaka Tomioka: demand was very high before the conflict involving Iran and is more likely to remain high than to strengthen further; prices are going up but procurement is not impossible, with uncertainty in some areas.
quarterly_data.figure: Supply concerns may arise between June and July (customer letters)

quarterly_data.signal: Medical and Pharmaceuticals and ICT&S (CEO / CFO): FY ended March 2026 Medical and Pharmaceuticals net sales rose 16% to approximately 36,400 million yen and operating income 147% to approximately 5,000 million yen; Taiyo Pharma Tech (contract manufacturing) net sales +30% as full-scale contract manufacturing for new customers started, Taiyo Pharma -4%, mystarz (dental prosthetics) +15%; ICT&S operating income approximately negative 95 million yen as scheduled sales at ICT group companies were delayed. FY ending March 2027: segment operating income -21% on sub-material, contracting and raw material inflation, cost impacts from technology transfer associated with the bankruptcy of neo CritiCare Pharma Co., Ltd., and the largest profit decrease at Taiyo Pharma Tech; the April 2026 NHI drug price revisions raise Taiyo Pharma's prices by an average in the low single-digit percentage range overall, but cost increases are larger and drug prices can only change on April 1, whereas Electronics can raise unit prices flexibly.
quarterly_data.figure: Medical and Pharmaceuticals FY ended March 2026: net sales approximately 36,400 million yen (+16%), operating income approximately 5,000 million yen (+147%); FY ending March 2027 operating income -21%
